Act I, 5 minutes. Context, not contribution: keep it moving and be out of this part at 05:00.
~60s. What matters for the rest of the talk: heterogeneity and volatility are what make a fixed deployment hard to keep working.
~45s. Bridge slide: these systems are the workload, the continuum is the substrate. The talk is about the mismatch between the two.
~70s. The row that matters is the last one: all three say what the collective computes, none of them says where it runs.
~60s. The research question of the thesis: say it slowly, everything after this answers it.
~60s. Roadmap: name the four blocks, then say the next ten minutes are mostly blocks 1 and 2. End of Act I, should be at 05:00.
Act II, 10 minutes, the core of the talk. Should end at 15:00.
~55s. In one sentence: keep the logical structure, dissolve the physical one.
~80s. Key slide. Behaviour is the computation, state is what persists between rounds, communication handles the neighbour exchange, sensors and actuators are bound to the hardware. Only the left group can move, and that constraint is what makes placement an interesting problem.
~60s. Left, what the program says; right, where it runs. The two are now independent. Sensors and actuators stay at the device tier.
~60s. Answer the obvious objection: if computation moves around, does the program still mean the same thing? Yes, and proving that is why the model is formalised.
~80s. Three papers on one slide. The point to make out loud: deployment control is itself a collective behaviour, so the same tools apply to it. Green planning is joint work with Brogi and Forti in Pisa.
~70s. Walk left to right, then the dashed feedback arrow. The novelty is the heterogeneous graph: earlier work flattens the topology and throws away the device diversity that makes placement hard.
~50s. Fill this slide. Once the figures are in, quote the headline numbers from each paper.
~65s. A whole thesis part on one slide, and say so. Framing: pulverisation says where code can run, these languages say how to write it so the compiler checks the placement. Mention TOPLAS is still under review.
~50s. Callback to the gap slide. End of Act II, should be at 15:00.
Act III, 5 minutes. This is a progress review: be concrete about what is done and what is left.
~55s. Do not read the table. Nine works, eight published or accepted, one under review at TOPLAS, and every thesis chapter has a paper behind it.
~90s. Progress review: the committee wants to know what is left, and it will ask for dates. Check the drafting state and put real months on the timeline before presenting.
~50s. Close on the last sentence, it is the one-line summary of the PhD.
